public_rationale: Marcus said LLMs were 'certainly' not reliable the way fictional general AIs are. OpenAI's own ChatGPT launch post (November 2022) says the model 'sometimes writes plausible-sounding but incorrect or nonsensical answers'. It also says the model gives different answers to slight rewordings of the same question. In December 2022, CEO Sam Altman warned that ChatGPT was not for reliable answers to factual questions. These statements by the leading developer, all dated before the post, support the claim that LLMs at the time were not reliable.
limitations: 'Reliably' is qualitative. The comparison is to fictional characters, so only the plain reading (frequent errors and inconsistency) is testable.
The evidence covers ChatGPT mainly, as the most prominent LLM at the time.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of January 2023, large language models such as ChatGPT were not reliable. They often gave wrong answers and behaved inconsistently, so they fell well short of the dependable general assistants of fiction.
The target period is from the ChatGPT launch (30 November 2022) to the post date. That was the most recent state of LLMs that public evidence could report on before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evidence, especially from the developers themselves, that leading LLMs in late 2022 and early 2023 often produced incorrect or inconsistent outputs and could not be relied on.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that leading LLMs at the time were consistently accurate and dependable across varied tasks.
